q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, no woman worker shall be required or allowed to work in a factory between the hours of:

options.A: 7 p.m. and 6 a.m.
options.B: 6 p.m. and 5 a.m.
options.C: 8 p.m. and 7 a.m.

e: Under the Factories Act, no woman worker shall be required or allowed to work in a factory between the hours of 7 p.m. and 6 a.m.

q: Under the Joint Consultative Machinery, the matters concerning railway employees generally, at the national level, are dealt with in:

options.A: The Permanent Negotiating Machinery at the Railway Board level
options.B: The Staff Council of the Zonal Railway
options.C: The National Council of the Joint Consultative Machinery alone

e: Under the Joint Consultative Machinery, matters concerning railway employees generally at the national level are dealt with in the Departmental Council (Railways).

q: In regard to Dearness Relief admissible to a railway pensioner who is re-employed in a Government office after his retirement, the correct position is that:

options.A: Dearness Relief is admissible to him in full during the period of his re-employment
options.B: Dearness Relief is not admissible to him during the period of his re-employment
options.C: Dearness Relief is admissible to him at 50 per cent of the normal rate during the period of re-employment
options.D: Dearness Relief is permanently forfeited as soon as he is re-employed

e: Dearness Relief is not admissible to a railway pensioner during the period of his re-employment in a Government office after retirement.

q: While disposing of an appeal under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, the appellate authority is required to consider, among other things:

options.A: Only the quantum of the penalty imposed on the appellant
options.B: Whether the penalty imposed on the appellant should be enhanced in every case
options.C: Whether the procedure prescribed in the rules has been complied with, whether the findings of the disciplinary authority are warranted by the evidence on record, and whether the penalty imposed is adequate, inadequate or severe
options.D: Only the recommendations made by the vigilance organisation in the case

e: While disposing of an appeal, the appellate authority must consider whether the prescribed procedure has been complied with, whether the findings of the disciplinary authority are warranted by the evidence on record, and whether the penalty imposed is adequate, inadequate or severe.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hospital Leave granted to a railway servant is not debited to the leave account of the railway servant.
2. Hospital Leave is admissible to every railway servant for any illness, whether or not it is connected with the discharge of his official duties.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: Hospital Leave is not debited to the leave account of the railway servant. Statement 2 is incorrect: it is admissible only for illness or injury connected with the discharge of official duties, not for any illness. Hence 1 only.

q:
Consider the following statements about the term "Pay" as defined in the Fundamental Rules:
1. "Pay" includes special pay and personal pay drawn by a railway servant.
2. "Pay" includes allowances such as House Rent Allowance and Transport Allowance admissible on the post.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: "Pay" as defined in the Fundamental Rules includes special pay and personal pay drawn by the railway servant. Statement 2 is incorrect: allowances such as House Rent Allowance and Transport Allowance do not form part of "pay". Hence 1 only.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 19,100 in Level 1 of the Pay Matrix is promoted to Level 2. His pay on promotion, fixed after granting one increment in Level 1 and placing him at the equal or next higher cell in Level 2, will be:
e: Working: 19,100 plus one increment in Level 1 gives 19,700; pay in Level 2 is fixed at the cell equal to, or next above, that amount, i.e. Rs 19,900.

q: Study leave is ordinarily granted to a railway servant for pursuing a course of study which:

options.A: May be on any subject of his personal choice, whether or not connected with his duties
options.B: Has a direct connection with the sphere of his duties, or is certified to be in public interest
options.C: Is confined only to preparation for departmental examinations
options.D: Is admissible only for studies abroad

e: Study leave is ordinarily granted for pursuing a course of study which has a direct connection with the sphere of the railway servant's duties, or is certified to be in public interest.

q: The average emoluments of a railway servant worked out to Rs 54,000. His monthly superannuation pension, at 50 per cent of average emoluments, will be:
e: Working: superannuation pension is 50 per cent of average emoluments: 50 per cent of Rs 54,000 = Rs 27,000 per month.

q:
Consider the following statements about voluntary retirement of a railway servant:
1. The notice of voluntary retirement requires acceptance by the appointing authority.
2. If the appointing authority does not refuse permission for retirement before the expiry of the period specified in the notice, the retirement becomes effective from the date of expiry of that period.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Both statements are correct: the notice of voluntary retirement requires acceptance by the appointing authority, and if permission is not refused before the expiry of the notice period, the retirement becomes effective from the date of expiry of that period.

q: A railway servant died in harness after completing 9 years of qualifying service, his emoluments being Rs 55,000. The death gratuity payable to his family (12 times of emoluments for service of 5 years or more but less than 11 years) will be:
e: Working: death gratuity for qualifying service of 5 years or more but less than 11 years is 12 times the emoluments: 12 x Rs 55,000 = Rs 6,60,000.

q: Rule 3(1)(iii) of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 requires every railway servant at all times to:

options.A: Maintain absolute integrity
options.B: Do nothing which is unbecoming of a railway servant
options.C: Take all possible steps to ensure the integrity of all railway servants under his control

e: Rule 3(1)(iii) of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 requires every railway servant at all times to do nothing which is unbecoming of a railway servant; integrity and devotion to duty are covered by the preceding clauses.

q: Under Rule 18 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, a railway servant shall not acquire or dispose of any immovable property by lease, mortgage, purchase, sale, gift or otherwise, except with the:

options.A: Previous knowledge of the prescribed authority
options.B: Previous sanction of the Railway Board in every case
options.C: No intimation or sanction is required in any case
options.D: Intimation to the prescribed authority within one year after the transaction

e: Under Rule 18 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, a railway servant shall not acquire or dispose of immovable property except with the previous knowledge of the prescribed authority.

q: A railway servant under NPS draws basic pay of Rs 44,000 and Dearness Allowance at 50 per cent of basic pay. The monthly contribution of the Government to his NPS account, at 14 per cent of basic pay plus DA, will be:
e: Working: Government contribution to NPS is 14 per cent of basic pay plus DA: 14 per cent of (44,000 + 22,000) = 14 per cent of Rs 66,000 = Rs 9,240.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, in regard to the weekly holiday of an adult worker, the correct position is:

options.A: He must be given a holiday on Sunday in every week, without any exception
options.B: He shall not be required to work on the first day of the week unless he has had, or will have, a holiday for a whole day on one of the three days immediately before or after that day
options.C: He is entitled to a holiday of two whole days in every week
options.D: The weekly holiday can be denied if overtime wages at double rate are paid

e: Under the Factories Act, an adult worker shall not be required to work on the first day of the week unless he has had, or will have, a holiday for a whole day on one of the three days immediately before or after that day.

q: A railway servant retired after 18 years of qualifying service with emoluments of Rs 58,000. His retirement gratuity, at one-fourth of emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of service, will be:
e: Working: retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments for each six-monthly period: Rs 14,500 x 36 periods (18 years) = Rs 5,22,000.

q: Under the RTI Act, 2005, a first appeal shall be disposed of by the First Appellate Authority within:

options.A: 30 days of receipt of the appeal, extendable up to a total of 45 days for reasons to be recorded in writing
options.B: 15 days of receipt of the appeal in all cases
options.C: 60 days of receipt of the appeal
options.D: 90 days of receipt of the appeal

e: Under the RTI Act, a first appeal shall be disposed of by the First Appellate Authority within 30 days of receipt, extendable up to a total of 45 days for reasons to be recorded in writing.

q: Both husband and wife are railway servants and are living together in a rented house; neither of them has been allotted Government accommodation. House Rent Allowance in this case is admissible to:

options.A: Only the husband
options.B: Both of them, each in his or her own right
options.C: Only the one who draws higher pay

e: Where both husband and wife are railway servants living together in a rented house and neither has been allotted Government accommodation, House Rent Allowance is admissible to both of them, each in his or her own right.

q: A deceased railway servant's last drawn pay was Rs 64,000. The enhanced rate of family pension, at 50 per cent of the last pay drawn, will be:
e: Working: enhanced family pension is 50 per cent of the last pay drawn: 50 per cent of Rs 64,000 = Rs 32,000 per month.

q:
Consider the following statements about nomination for Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity:
1. A railway servant may, in his nomination, specify an alternate nominee who becomes entitled to the gratuity if the nominee predeceases him.
2. A nomination for DCRG takes effect only from the date of retirement of the railway servant.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: a nominee may be supported by an alternate nominee who becomes entitled to the gratuity if the nominee predeceases the railway servant. Statement 2 is incorrect: a DCRG nomination does not take effect only from retirement. Hence 1 only.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, no child who has not completed the age of ______ shall be required or allowed to work in any factory.

options.A: 12 years
options.B: 15 years
options.C: 14 years

e: Under the Factories Act, no child who has not completed the age of 14 years shall be required or allowed to work in any factory.

q: A railway servant retired with 90 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement was Rs 48,000 and Dearness Allowance was admissible at 50 per cent of basic pay. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him will be:
e: Working: cash equivalent = (pay + DA) divided by 30 x days of leave: (48,000 + 24,000) / 30 x 90 = Rs 2,400 x 90 = Rs 2,16,000.

q: Under the RTI Act, 2005, the first appeal against a decision of the Central Public Information Officer lies to:

options.A: The Central Public Information Officer himself
options.B: An officer senior in rank to the Central Public Information Officer in the public authority
options.C: The Head of Office in all cases

e: Under the RTI Act, the first appeal against a decision of the Central Public Information Officer lies to an officer senior in rank to the CPIO within the same public authority.

q: Honorarium cannot be granted to a railway servant for work which:

options.A: Forms part of his normal and routine duties
options.B: Is of an occasional or intermittent character
options.C: Is of a special nature involving higher responsibility
options.D: Is performed beyond office hours with the permission of the competent authority

e: Honorarium is admissible only for work of an occasional, intermittent or special nature; it cannot be granted for work which forms part of the railway servant's normal and routine duties.

q: A railway servant superannuates under the Unified Pension Scheme after 26 years of qualifying service. His last drawn basic pay was Rs 60,000 and Dearness Allowance was 50 per cent of basic pay. The lump sum payable to him, at one-tenth of his last drawn monthly emoluments (basic pay + DA) for every completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Working: lump sum is one-tenth of last drawn basic pay plus DA for each six-monthly period: Rs 9,000 x 52 periods (26 years) = Rs 4,68,000.

q: Under the Hours of Employment Regulations, an employment is classified as "Essentially Intermittent" when:

options.A: The work is of a continuous nature requiring constant and sustained attention
options.B: The duties are of a supervisory or confidential nature
options.C: The daily duty hours include long periods of inaction, during which the staff is required to be on duty but is not called upon to perform active work, interspersed with short spells of activity
options.D: The work is performed only during night hours

e: Under the Hours of Employment Regulations, employment is Essentially Intermittent when the daily duty hours include long periods of inaction, during which the staff is required to be on duty but is not called upon to perform active work, interspersed with short spells of activity.

q: A Group "B" gazetted railway servant who accepts a gift from a near relative or a personal friend, having no official dealings with him, on a ceremonial occasion like a wedding, is required to report the gift to the prescribed authority if its value exceeds:
e: A Group B gazetted railway servant must report to the prescribed authority a gift from a near relative or personal friend on a ceremonial occasion if its value exceeds Rs 15,000.

q: The last pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 1,00,000. The normal rate of family pension, at 30 per cent of the last pay drawn, will be:
e: Working: family pension at the normal rate is 30 per cent of the last pay drawn: 30 per cent of Rs 1,00,000 = Rs 30,000 per month.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, where the employment of a person is terminated, the wages earned by him shall be paid:

options.A: On the seventh day after termination
options.B: Before the expiry of the second working day from the day on which his employment is terminated
options.C: On the tenth day after termination
options.D: Along with the wages of the next wage period

e: Under the Payment of Wages Act, where employment is terminated, the wages earned shall be paid before the expiry of the second working day from the day on which the employment is terminated.

q: Confirmation of a railway servant in a post is made:

options.A: Automatically on the expiry of the period of probation
options.B: Only on the recommendation of the Union Public Service Commission
options.C: Against an available permanent (substantive) vacancy, after satisfactory completion of the period of probation
options.D: Only at the time of his promotion to a higher post

e: Confirmation of a railway servant is made against an available permanent (substantive) vacancy, after satisfactory completion of the period of probation; it is not automatic on the expiry of probation.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 38,000 applies for House Building Advance for purchasing a ready-built house costing Rs 70 lakh. The maximum advance admissible to him, at 139 times his basic pay or the cost of the house, whichever is less, will be:
e: Working: House Building Advance is limited to 139 times basic pay or the cost of the house, whichever is less: 139 x Rs 38,000 = Rs 52,82,000, which is less than the cost of Rs 70 lakh.

q: Under Section 6(2) of the RTI Act, 2005, an applicant making a request for information:

options.A: Is not required to give any reason for requesting the information, or any personal details other than those necessary for contacting him
options.B: Must state in detail the reasons for seeking the information
options.C: Must disclose his personal particulars in all cases
options.D: Must first obtain the permission of the First Appellate Authority

e: Under Section 6(2) of the RTI Act, an applicant is not required to give any reason for requesting the information, or any personal details other than those necessary for contacting him.

q: The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to a railway servant on retirement, in respect of Leave on Average Pay at his credit, is computed as:

options.A: Pay multiplied by the number of days of leave, divided by 365
options.B: Pay plus Dearness Allowance admissible on the date of retirement, divided by 30 and multiplied by the number of days of leave at credit
options.C: Pay plus all allowances including House Rent Allowance, divided by 30 and multiplied by the number of days of leave at credit
options.D: Pay divided by 26 and multiplied by the number of days of leave at credit

e: Cash equivalent of leave salary is computed by dividing pay plus Dearness Allowance admissible on the date of retirement by 30 and multiplying by the number of days of Leave on Average Pay at credit; other allowances are not included.

q: A railway pensioner has attained the age of 90 years. His basic pension is Rs 38,000. The additional quantum of pension admissible to him, at 40 per cent of the basic pension, will be:
e: Working: the additional quantum of pension at the age of 90 years is 40 per cent of the basic pension: 40 per cent of Rs 38,000 = Rs 15,200 per month.

q: Which of the following is admissible to a railway servant on transfer in public interest, in addition to the Composite Transfer Grant?

options.A: Reimbursement of the charges for transportation of personal effects and conveyance, as part of Travelling Allowance
options.B: A second Composite Transfer Grant for his family
options.C: Daily allowance for an unlimited period of stay at the new station
options.D: Reimbursement of the cost of constructing a house at the new station

e: On transfer in public interest, in addition to the Composite Transfer Grant, reimbursement of charges for transportation of personal effects and conveyance is admissible as part of Travelling Allowance.

q: Information including commercial confidence, trade secrets or intellectual property, the disclosure of which would harm the competitive position of a third party, is exempt from disclosure under which provision of the RTI Act, 2005?

options.A: Section 8(1)(a)
options.B: Section 8(1)(i)
options.C: Section 8(1)(d)

e: Information including commercial confidence, trade secrets or intellectual property, the disclosure of which would harm the competitive position of a third party, is exempt from disclosure under Section 8(1)(d) of the RTI Act.

q: A railway servant's pension is Rs 55,000 per month. He commutes 40 per cent of his pension. Taking the commutation value for age on the next birthday as 8.194, the lump sum commuted value payable to him will be:
e: Working: monthly pension commuted = 40 per cent of Rs 55,000 = Rs 22,000; commuted value = 22,000 x 12 x 8.194 = Rs 21,63,216.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, a deduction from wages for damage to, or loss of, goods expressly entrusted to the employed person can be made only after:

options.A: Obtaining the approval of the Accounts Officer
options.B: Giving the employed person an opportunity of showing cause against the deduction
options.C: Obtaining the order of the General Manager
options.D: Obtaining the consent of the recognised trade union

e: Under the Payment of Wages Act, a deduction for damage to, or loss of, goods expressly entrusted to the employed person can be made only after giving him an opportunity of showing cause against the deduction.

q: In regard to House Rent Allowance during the period of suspension of a railway servant, the correct position is:

options.A: It is not admissible at all during suspension
options.B: It is admissible only at half the normal rate
options.C: It is admissible only for the first 90 days of suspension
options.D: It continues to be admissible, subject to the prescribed conditions, at the rate drawn immediately before suspension

e: House Rent Allowance continues to be admissible during the period of suspension, subject to the prescribed conditions, at the rate drawn immediately before suspension.

q: A railway servant retired with 8 years of qualifying service, which is less than 10 years, and is accordingly granted service gratuity in lieu of pension. His emoluments were Rs 40,000. The service gratuity payable to him, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Working: service gratuity is half a month's emoluments for each six-monthly period: Rs 20,000 x 16 periods (8 years) = Rs 3,20,000.

q: An order of suspension passed against a railway servant under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules may be revoked at any time by:

options.A: The Railway Board only
options.B: The appellate authority only
options.C: The authority which made the order, or any authority to which that authority is subordinate

e: An order of suspension under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules may be revoked at any time by the authority which made the order, or by any authority to which that authority is subordinate.

q: Children Education Allowance is admissible in respect of a child (other than a Divyang child) up to:

options.A: The age of 20 years or passing of Class XII, whichever is earlier
options.B: The age of 18 years in all cases
options.C: The age of 22 years or passing of Class XII, whichever is earlier
options.D: There is no age limit so long as the child is studying

e: Children Education Allowance in respect of a child other than a Divyang child is admissible up to the age of 20 years or the passing of Class XII, whichever is earlier.

q: A railway servant drawing last basic pay of Rs 62,000 is transferred in public interest and changes his residence. The Composite Transfer Grant admissible to him, at 80 per cent of his last drawn basic pay, will be:
e: Working: Composite Transfer Grant is 80 per cent of the last basic pay: 80 per cent of Rs 62,000 = Rs 49,600.

q: In a departmental inquiry under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, the charged railway servant is entitled to:

options.A: Examine the disciplinary authority as a witness
options.B: Cross-examine the witnesses produced in support of the charges
options.C: Summon any person as a witness of his choice

e: In a departmental inquiry, the charged railway servant is entitled to cross-examine the witnesses produced in support of the charges against him.

q: The standard of distant vision prescribed for the Aye-Two (A-2) medical category for railway servants is:

options.A: 6/6, 6/6 without glasses
options.B: 6/12, 6/12 with or without glasses
options.C: 6/9, 6/9 with or without glasses

e: The standard of distant vision prescribed for the Aye-Two (A-2) medical category is 6/9, 6/9 with or without glasses.

q: Dress Allowance admissible to eligible railway servants is paid once in a year, in the month of:

options.A: January
options.B: April
options.C: October

e: Dress Allowance admissible to eligible railway servants is paid once in a year, in the month of July.

q: Where a retired railway servant dies before receiving the amount of retirement gratuity sanctioned to him, the gratuity amount is:

options.A: Paid to his nominee or, where no nomination subsists, to his family in accordance with the rules
options.B: Lapsed to the Government in all cases
options.C: Paid to the bank through which pension was drawn
options.D: Necessarily adjusted against Government dues before any payment

e: Where a retired railway servant dies before receiving the retirement gratuity sanctioned to him, the amount is paid to his nominee or, where no nomination subsists, to his family in accordance with the rules; it does not lapse to the Government.

q: Ad hoc bonus, admissible to RPF/RPSF personnel who are not covered by the Productivity Linked Bonus scheme, is computed as the equivalent of wages for:

options.A: 78 days
options.B: 60 days
options.C: 30 days

e: Ad hoc bonus admissible to RPF/RPSF personnel not covered by the Productivity Linked Bonus scheme is computed as the equivalent of wages for 30 days.

q: The lump sum commuted value of pension payable to a railway pensioner is calculated as:

options.A: The monthly pension multiplied by the commutation factor
options.B: The annual pension multiplied by the commutation factor
options.C: The amount of monthly pension commuted, multiplied by 12 and by the commutation value (factor) for the age on the next birthday

e: The lump sum commuted value of pension is the amount of monthly pension commuted, multiplied by 12 and by the commutation value (factor) for the age on the next birthday.

q: Where a notice is issued to a third party under Section 11 of the RTI Act, 2005, the Central Public Information Officer shall make a decision on disclosure of the information within:

options.A: 30 days after receipt of the request
options.B: 35 days after receipt of the request
options.C: 45 days after receipt of the request
options.D: 40 days after receipt of the request

e: Where notice is issued to a third party under Section 11 of the RTI Act, the Central Public Information Officer shall decide on disclosure of the information within 40 days after receipt of the request.

q: For the purpose of House Rent Allowance, a city is classified as 'Z' class if its population is:

options.A: 50 lakh and above
options.B: 25 lakh and above but below 50 lakh
options.C: Below 5 lakh
options.D: 10 lakh and above but below 25 lakh

e: Under the 7th CPC HRA classification, cities are classed X (50 lakh and above), Y (5 lakh to below 50 lakh) and Z (below 5 lakh), so a city below 5 lakh population is Z class.

q: A railway servant on tour is provided with free boarding only, the lodging being arranged and paid for by himself. The Daily Allowance admissible to him for that day will be:

options.A: 25% of the Daily Allowance
options.B: 75% of the Daily Allowance
options.C: 50% of the Daily Allowance

e: Daily Allowance has boarding and lodging components. Where free boarding only is provided and the servant pays for lodging himself, 50 percent of the Daily Allowance is admissible under the TA Rules.

q: The monthly subscription payable by a Group 'D' railway servant under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme is:

options.A: Rs 15 per month
options.B: Rs 30 per month
options.C: Rs 60 per month

e: Under CGEGIS, the monthly subscription is graded by group: Group D (now Level-1) pays Rs 15 per month, Group C Rs 30, Group B Rs 60 and Group A Rs 120.

q: A privilege pass issued to a railway servant remains valid for a period of:

options.A: One month from the date of issue
options.B: Two months from the date of issue
options.C: Three months from the date of issue
options.D: Five months from the date of issue

e: A privilege pass issued to a railway servant is valid for five months from the date of issue, within which the outward and return journeys must be completed, as per the Railway Servants (Pass) Rules.

q: A Residential Card Pass issued to a railway servant entitles him to:

options.A: Travel on duty anywhere on the Railways without a duty pass
options.B: Travel between the station of his residence and the station of his duty, where he resides at a station other than his headquarters
options.C: Travel with his family on privilege account once a year
options.D: Travel in a higher class than his entitlement on payment of the difference of fare

e: A Residential Card Pass is issued when a railway servant resides at a station other than his headquarters; it entitles him to travel between his residence station and his duty station.

q: A School Pass on the Railways is issued in favour of:

options.A: Railway servants attending a departmental training school
options.B: Teachers employed in railway schools for their official tours
options.C: The son or daughter of a railway servant studying at an outstation, to travel between the station of the school and the headquarters or residence of the railway servant during vacations
options.D: Railway servants for appearing in a departmental examination

e: A School Pass is issued for the son or daughter of a railway servant studying at an outstation, to travel between the school station and the headquarters or residence of the servant during vacations.

q: A Duty Pass is issued to a railway servant to enable him to:

options.A: Travel on official duty in connection with railway work
options.B: Travel with his family to his home town on leave
options.C: Travel after retirement to his place of settlement
options.D: Travel for appearing as a witness in a court in a private case

e: A Duty Pass is issued to enable a railway servant to travel on official duty in connection with railway work, as distinct from privilege or complimentary passes.

q: Privilege passes and complimentary passes on the Railways are now ordinarily issued to railway servants:

options.A: Only in paper form by the pass issuing authority
options.B: By the Accounts Office along with the pay bill
options.C: Online, as e-passes, through the e-pass module of the Human Resource Management System (HRMS)
options.D: By the Railway Recruitment Board on application

e: Privilege and complimentary passes are now ordinarily issued online as e-passes through the e-pass module of HRMS, replacing the earlier manual paper pass system.

q: Metal token passes on the Railways are issued to:

options.A: All non-gazetted railway servants
options.B: Group 'A' and Group 'B' gazetted railway officers
options.C: Only railway servants in Level-1
options.D: Only members of the Railway Board

e: Metal token passes, which serve as a standing authority to travel, are issued only to Group A and Group B gazetted railway officers.

q: The maximum number of partial withdrawals permitted to a subscriber from his Tier-I account under the National Pension System before attaining the age of 60 years is:

options.A: One
options.B: Two
options.C: Five

e: A maximum of 4 partial withdrawals are now permitted before age 60/superannuation (with a 4-year gap between withdrawals). (Source: PFRDA (Exits and Withdrawals under NPS) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025, notified 16.12.2025; PIB Release ID 2206763 dated 19.12.2025.)

q: Family pension payable to a childless widow of a deceased railway servant who remarries is:

options.A: Payable after her remarriage if her income from all other sources does not exceed the amount of minimum family pension plus dearness relief admissible thereon
options.B: Stopped in all cases on her remarriage
options.C: Payable only till she attains the age of 60 years
options.D: Payable only if she has no son or daughter

e: Under the RS (Pension) Rules, family pension to a childless widow continues even after remarriage if her income from all other sources does not exceed minimum family pension plus dearness relief thereon.

q: A brother or sister of a deceased railway servant who is suffering from a disorder or disability of mind, or is physically disabled so as to be unable to earn a livelihood, and who was wholly dependent on the railway servant, is eligible for family pension:

options.A: Only up to the age of 25 years
options.B: Not at all, as only the spouse and children are eligible
options.C: Only if the deceased has left no son or daughter
options.D: For his or her lifetime, subject to the prescribed conditions

e: A dependent brother or sister who is disabled or suffering from a disorder of mind and was wholly dependent on the deceased is eligible for family pension for life, subject to the prescribed conditions, under the RS (Pension) Rules.

q: Hostel subsidy under the Children Education Allowance scheme is admissible only where the hostel in which the child is residing is situated at a distance from the residence of the railway servant of at least:

options.A: 10 kilometres
options.B: 50 kilometres
options.C: 100 kilometres
options.D: There is no condition regarding distance

e: Hostel subsidy under CEA is admissible only if the hostel is situated at least 50 kilometres from the residence of the railway servant.

q: Quarantine leave granted to a railway servant, which is ordinarily limited to 21 days at a time, may in exceptional circumstances be extended up to:

options.A: 21 days in all cases, with no provision for extension
options.B: 45 days
options.C: 30 days, on the certificate of the competent medical or public health authority

e: Quarantine leave is ordinarily limited to 21 days at a time, but may be extended up to 30 days in exceptional circumstances on the certificate of the competent medical or public health authority, per IREM.

q: A female railway servant is granted Special Maternity Leave in case of a still birth or the death of her child soon after its birth. The duration of such leave is:

options.A: 60 days
options.B: 30 days
options.C: 45 days

e: Special Maternity Leave of 60 days is admissible to a female railway servant in case of still birth or death of the child soon after birth, as per the leave rules in IREM.

q: Work Related Illness and Injury Leave granted to a railway servant carries full leave salary for the period of his hospitalisation. For the period of leave beyond hospitalisation, the leave salary admissible is:

options.A: Full pay for the entire period of the leave
options.B: No leave salary at all
options.C: The leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay
options.D: Equal to the leave salary admissible during Leave on Half Average Pay

e: Under Work Related Illness and Injury Leave, full leave salary is paid during hospitalisation; beyond hospitalisation, leave salary equals that admissible during Leave on Half Average Pay.

q: Special Casual Leave admissible to a female railway servant for the insertion of an Intra-Uterine Device (IUD) for family planning is:

options.A: Half a day
options.B: One day
options.C: Six days

e: Special Casual Leave of one day is admissible to a female railway servant for insertion of an Intra-Uterine Device for family planning.

q: A railway servant drawing pay of Rs 60,000 per month is placed under suspension. The subsistence allowance payable to him, exclusive of dearness allowance admissible thereon, will be:

options.A: Rs 60,000 per month
options.B: Rs 15,000 per month
options.C: Rs 30,000 per month

e: Subsistence allowance during suspension equals leave salary on Leave on Half Average Pay, i.e. half of pay: Rs 60,000 x 1/2 = Rs 30,000 per month, plus DA thereon.

q: A railway servant availed Extra Ordinary Leave for 100 days during a half-year. The Leave on Average Pay to be credited in advance to his leave account at the beginning of the succeeding half-year, after applying the prescribed reduction for such leave, will be:

options.A: 5 days
options.B: 15 days
options.C: 10 days

e: LAP credit is 15 days per half-year, reduced by one-tenth of EOL availed, subject to a maximum reduction of 15 days: 15 - (100/10) = 15 - 10 = 5 days.

q: Creation of a new gazetted post on a zonal Railway requires the sanction of:

options.A: The Divisional Railway Manager
options.B: The General Manager alone
options.C: The Principal Financial Adviser

e: Creation of a new gazetted post on a zonal Railway requires the sanction of the Railway Board; the General Manager has no such power for gazetted posts.

q: In manpower planning on the Railways, 'benchmarking' of staff strength means:

options.A: Laying down a fixed yardstick for every activity in all units uniformly
options.B: Identifying, among comparable units, the most economical deployment of staff for an activity and adopting that deployment as the standard to be achieved by other units
options.C: Surrendering a fixed percentage of posts every year
options.D: Freezing all vacancies in a cadre for a prescribed period

e: Benchmarking in manpower planning means identifying, among comparable units, the most economical staff deployment for an activity and adopting it as the standard for other units to achieve.

q: The Unique Medical Identity (UMID) card on the Railways is issued to:

options.A: Serving railway employees, railway pensioners and their eligible family members and dependents
options.B: Only railway pensioners
options.C: Only serving railway employees
options.D: Only personnel of the Railway Protection Force

e: The UMID card is issued to serving railway employees, railway pensioners and their eligible family members and dependents for cashless medical treatment.

q: The two recognised federations of railway employees which participate in the Permanent Negotiating Machinery at the Railway Board level are:

options.A: The recognised staff councils of the zonal railways
options.B: The officers' associations of the zonal railways
options.C: The unions recognised only at the divisional level
options.D: The All India Railwaymen's Federation and the National Federation of Indian Railwaymen

e: AIRF and NFIR are the two recognised federations participating in the Permanent Negotiating Machinery at Railway Board level.

q: Reservation for ex-servicemen in direct recruitment to Group 'C' posts on the Railways is:

options.A: 20% of the vacancies
options.B: 10% of the vacancies
options.C: 5% of the vacancies

e: Reservation for ex-servicemen in direct recruitment to Group C posts on the Railways is 10 percent of the vacancies.

q: Which of the following advances admissible earlier to railway servants stands abolished under the 7th CPC dispensation?

options.A: House Building Advance
options.B: Personal Computer Advance
options.C: Bicycle Advance

e: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, Bicycle Advance stands abolished, while House Building Advance, Personal Computer Advance and Flood Advance continue.

q: Constant Attendant Allowance admissible to a railway pensioner granted pension on account of 100% disablement, who requires the services of an attendant, is payable at the rate of:

options.A: Rs 8,438 per month
options.B: Rs 1,000 per month
options.C: Rs 3,000 per month

e: Constant Attendant Allowance is Rs 6,750 per month, increased by 25 percent when DA crossed 50 percent: Rs 6,750 x 1.25 = Rs 8,438 per month (rounded).

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, first-aid boxes, with the prescribed contents, must be provided and maintained at the rate of not less than:

options.A: One for every 50 workers ordinarily employed
options.B: One for every 100 workers ordinarily employed
options.C: One for every 200 workers ordinarily employed
options.D: One for every 150 workers ordinarily employed

e: Section 45 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires first-aid boxes at not less than one for every 150 workers ordinarily employed in the factory.

q: Information, the disclosure of which would prejudicially affect the sovereignty and integrity of India or the security of the State, is exempt from disclosure under the Right to Information Act, 2005 under:

options.A: Section 8(1)(d)
options.B: Section 8(1)(a)
options.C: Section 8(1)(j)

e: Section 8(1)(a) of the RTI Act, 2005 exempts information whose disclosure would prejudicially affect the sovereignty and integrity of India or the security of the State.

q: Under Section 7(9) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, information sought by an applicant shall ordinarily be provided:

options.A: In the form in which it is sought in every case, without any exception
options.B: Only in printed form, whatever form is sought by the applicant
options.C: In the form in which it is sought, unless that would disproportionately divert the resources of the public authority or be detrimental to the safety or preservation of the record
options.D: Only in electronic form through e-mail

e: Section 7(9) of the RTI Act provides that information shall ordinarily be given in the form sought, unless it would disproportionately divert resources or harm the safety or preservation of the record.

q: 'Average pay', as defined in the Fundamental Rules applicable to railway servants, means:

options.A: The average monthly pay earned during the twelve complete months immediately preceding the month in which the event requiring its calculation occurs
options.B: The pay drawn by the railway servant in the last month of his service
options.C: The average monthly pay earned during the last ten months of service
options.D: The average monthly pay earned during the last three years of service

e: Under the Fundamental Rules, average pay means the average monthly pay earned during the twelve complete months immediately preceding the month in which the event requiring its calculation occurs.

q: Consultation with the Union Public Service Commission on disciplinary matters affecting a person serving under the Government in a civil capacity is provided for in the Constitution under:

options.A: Article 311
options.B: Article 309
options.C: Article 312

e: Article 320(3)(c) of the Constitution requires consultation with the UPSC on disciplinary matters affecting a person serving in a civil capacity.

q: Railway servants borne in the 'Aye' medical categories, whose duties are connected with train running, are additionally required to:

options.A: Undergo no test other than a test of distant vision
options.B: Pass the prescribed test for colour perception (colour vision)
options.C: Undergo a colour vision test only at the time of retirement
options.D: Undergo a colour vision test only if they are Loco Pilots

e: Railway servants in the Aye medical categories connected with train running must additionally pass the prescribed colour perception (colour vision) test.

q: The standard of distant vision prescribed for the 'Bee-One' (B-1) medical category on the Railways is:

options.A: 6/6, 6/6 without glasses
options.B: 6/9, 6/9 without glasses
options.C: 6/9, 6/12 with or without glasses

e: The B-1 (Bee-One) medical category prescribes distant vision of 6/9, 6/12 with or without glasses.

q: In regard to the Annual Performance Appraisal Report of a railway servant, the correct position is that the railway servant:

options.A: May submit a representation against the entries and grading in his report to the competent authority within the prescribed period
options.B: Can make no representation of any kind against his report
options.C: May represent only to the President of India
options.D: Is never shown his report in any circumstances

e: The railway servant is entitled to submit a representation against the entries and grading in his APAR to the competent authority within the prescribed period.

q: Where a railway servant on deputation to an ex-cadre post opts for the pay of his parent cadre post plus Deputation (Duty) Allowance, the governing condition is that:

options.A: There is no ceiling on the total amount so drawn by him
options.B: The sum of his basic pay and the Deputation (Duty) Allowance shall not exceed the maximum of the pay level prescribed for the ex-cadre post
options.C: The Deputation (Duty) Allowance is payable in addition, without any relation to his basic pay
options.D: He must draw only the Deputation (Duty) Allowance and no basic pay

e: On deputation, where the servant opts for parent cadre pay plus Deputation (Duty) Allowance, basic pay plus the allowance must not exceed the maximum of the pay level prescribed for the ex-cadre post.

q: A railway pensioner who has joined the Retired Employees Liberalised Health Scheme may avail treatment in a recognised or empanelled private hospital:

options.A: In no circumstances, treatment being confined to railway hospitals alone
options.B: Only after his retirement benefits are finally settled by the Accounts Office
options.C: Only if he surrenders his Fixed Medical Allowance for the whole year in advance
options.D: In an emergency, or on being referred for the purpose, in accordance with the prescribed procedure

e: A pensioner under RELHS may avail treatment in a recognised or empanelled private hospital in an emergency, or on referral, following the prescribed procedure.

q: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, the Government's contribution of 18.5% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance to the corpus of a subscriber is credited as under:

options.A: 14% to the individual corpus and 4.5% to the pool corpus
options.B: 10% to the individual corpus and 8.5% to the pool corpus
options.C: The entire 18.5% to the individual corpus of the subscriber
options.D: 8.5% to the individual corpus and 10% to the pool corpus

e: Under UPS, of the Government contribution of 18.5 percent of Basic Pay plus DA, 10 percent goes to the individual corpus and 8.5 percent to the pool corpus.

q: A stagnation increment granted to a railway servant who has reached the maximum of his pay level is:

options.A: Counted for no purpose at all
options.B: Counted only for the purpose of Dearness Allowance
options.C: Treated as pay for all purposes, including pensionary benefits
options.D: Granted as personal pay and absorbed in the next increment

e: A stagnation increment is treated as pay for all purposes, including pensionary benefits, and is not mere personal pay.

q: In regard to joining time admissible to a railway servant on transfer in public interest, the correct position is that joining time:

options.A: May be combined with any kind of leave due and admissible to the railway servant
options.B: Can never be combined with any kind of leave
options.C: Can be combined only with casual leave
options.D: Is forfeited if the railway servant avails any leave during the journey

e: Joining time on transfer in public interest may be combined with any kind of leave due and admissible to the railway servant.

q: The obligation of every public authority to publish, suo motu, the particulars of its organisation, functions and duties, and the other prescribed particulars, is laid down in the Right to Information Act, 2005 in:

options.A: Section 6
options.B: Section 7
options.C: Section 11

e: Section 4 of the RTI Act, 2005 obliges every public authority to publish suo motu the particulars of its organisation, functions, duties and other prescribed particulars.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a child worker who has worked for the prescribed qualifying period in a factory is entitled to leave with wages in the subsequent year at the rate of:

options.A: One day for every 20 days of work performed by him
options.B: One day for every 15 days of work performed by him
options.C: One day for every 10 days of work performed by him
options.D: One day for every 25 days of work performed by him

e: Section 79 of the Factories Act entitles a child worker to leave with wages at one day for every 15 days of work performed, as against one for 20 days for adults.

q: A gateman whose rostered duty consists of long periods of inaction, during which he is required to be on duty but is not called upon to perform active work, interspersed with short spells of activity when trains pass, is classified under the Hours of Employment Regulations as:

options.A: Intensive
options.B: Continuous
options.C: Essentially Intermittent

e: Under HOER, work with long periods of inaction interspersed with short spells of activity, as with a gateman, is classified as Essentially Intermittent.

q: A railway pensioner who had commuted a portion of his pension dies before the expiry of the period of restoration of the commuted portion. In regard to the unrecovered commuted value, the correct position is that:

options.A: It is not recovered from the family pension payable to his family
options.B: It is recovered in full from the family pension
options.C: One-half of it is recovered from the family pension
options.D: Family pension is not payable until it is fully recovered

e: The unrecovered commuted value of pension is not recovered from family pension; on the pensioner's death, recovery from the family is barred under the commutation rules.

q: A temporary (refundable) advance drawn by a railway servant from the amount at his credit in the Provident Fund may subsequently be:

options.A: Never altered in its character in any circumstances
options.B: Converted automatically into a final withdrawal on the expiry of one year
options.C: Converted into a final withdrawal only after the retirement of the railway servant
options.D: Converted into a final (non-refundable) withdrawal, subject to the prescribed conditions and limits

e: A temporary PF advance may be converted into a final (non-refundable) withdrawal, subject to the prescribed conditions and limits, under the Provident Fund rules in IREM.

q: The amount at the credit of a Government subscriber in his Tier-I account under the National Pension System is invested:

options.A: Directly by the Accounts Office of the Railway in which he is serving
options.B: Only in Government securities by the Central Recordkeeping Agency
options.C: Through Pension Fund Managers, in accordance with the investment pattern and guidelines prescribed for Government subscribers
options.D: By keeping it as a deposit in the bank account of the subscriber

e: Tier-I accumulations of a Government NPS subscriber are invested through Pension Fund Managers as per the investment pattern and guidelines prescribed for Government subscribers.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Unified Pension Scheme:
1. Where the individual corpus of a subscriber at superannuation is less than the benchmark corpus, the assured payout admissible to him is proportionately reduced.
2. The whole of the Government's contribution of 18.5% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance is credited to the individual corpus of the subscriber.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Under UPS the assured payout is proportionately reduced if the individual corpus is below the benchmark corpus, so statement 1 is correct; statement 2 is wrong as only 10 percent of the Government contribution goes to the individual corpus, the rest to the pool corpus.

q: Information available to a person in his fiduciary relationship is exempt from disclosure under the Right to Information Act, 2005 under:

options.A: Section 8(1)(d)
options.B: Section 8(1)(j)
options.C: Section 8(1)(e)

e: Section 8(1)(e) of the RTI Act exempts information available to a person in his fiduciary relationship, unless larger public interest warrants disclosure.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 20,500 in Level 2 of the pay matrix is promoted to a post in Level 3. One increment is first granted to him in Level 2, taking his pay to the next cell of Rs 21,100, and his pay is then fixed in Level 3 at the cell equal to, or next above, that amount. His basic pay in Level 3 will be:
e: One increment in Level 2 takes pay from Rs 20,500 to Rs 21,100; in Level 3 the cell equal to or next above Rs 21,100 is Rs 21,700, so pay is fixed at Rs 21,700 under FR 22.

q: An employment is classified as 'Intensive' under the Hours of Employment Regulations when the work involved is of a nature that:

options.A: Consists of long periods of inaction interspersed with short spells of activity
options.B: Is of a supervisory or confidential nature
options.C: Is performed only during the night hours
options.D: Involves continuous and sustained attention and strenuous effort, with little or no period of relaxation

e: Under HOER, Intensive employment involves continuous and sustained attention and strenuous effort with little or no period of relaxation.

q: Dearness Allowance payable to railway servants is revised from time to time with reference to the movement of the:

options.A: All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers
options.B: Wholesale Price Index
options.C: Consumer Price Index for Urban Non-Manual Employees
options.D: Cost Inflation Index notified under the Income-tax Act

e: Dearness Allowance for railway servants is revised with reference to the All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (AICPI-IW).
